questions.question: Which limit defines the directional derivative $\mathrm{D}_{\boldsymbol{v}}\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$?
questions.explanation: The directional derivative is the one-sided limit of the difference quotient along $\boldsymbol{v}$: $\mathrm{D}_{\boldsymbol{v}}\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)=\lim_{t\to0^+}\frac{\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0+t\boldsymbol{v})-\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)}{t}$.
questions.source_support: The definition displays the limit for $\mathrm{D}_{\boldsymbol{v}}\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$.

$t\to\infty$ is the wrong limit; the difference quotient needs $t\to0^+$.
$\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0+t)$ omits the division by $t$ and drops the $\boldsymbol{v}$ direction.
